difficultyRationale: Tests the actual precedence rule between local and global exception handlers, which candidates frequently get backwards or assume is configurable only by ordering annotations.
prompt: A controller has its own `@ExceptionHandler(IllegalArgumentException.class)` method. A separate `@ControllerAdvice`-annotated class also declares an `@ExceptionHandler(IllegalArgumentException.class)` method intended to apply globally. When a handler method in that controller throws an `IllegalArgumentException`, which handler runs, and why?
explanation: Spring MVC resolves `@ExceptionHandler` methods by searching the controller that threw the exception first, and only falls back to `@ControllerAdvice` beans if no matching handler is found locally. An exception handler declared directly in the controller is therefore always preferred over one declared in a `@ControllerAdvice`, regardless of the advice's own ordering (`@Order` or `Ordered`) relative to other advice beans — ordering only decides precedence among multiple applicable `@ControllerAdvice` beans, not between a local handler and any advice.

options.text: Whichever handler carries the lower `@Order` value runs, since Spring MVC's `@ExceptionHandler` resolution always ranks candidates by `@Order` across both local controller handlers and global `@ControllerAdvice` handlers alike.
options.explanation: `@Order` governs precedence among multiple `@ControllerAdvice` beans when more than one could apply; it does not come into play between a controller's own local handler and any advice, since the local handler is checked first and wins outright.

options.text: Both the local handler and the `@ControllerAdvice` handler run, one after the other in an unspecified order, because Spring MVC does not deduplicate multiple applicable handlers for the same exception type.
options.explanation: Spring MVC resolves exactly one `@ExceptionHandler` method for a given thrown exception per request — it does not invoke multiple matching handlers for the same exception.

options.text: Neither handler runs at all; declaring both a local `@ExceptionHandler` and a global `@ControllerAdvice` handler for the same exception type is rejected as an ambiguous configuration error at application startup.
options.explanation: Declaring the same exception type in both a local `@ExceptionHandler` and a `@ControllerAdvice` is valid and does not fail at startup; Spring MVC simply has a precedence rule for which one applies at request time.

options.text: The controller's own local `@ExceptionHandler` method runs, because Spring MVC looks for a matching handler in the controller that threw the exception before considering any `@ControllerAdvice`.
options.explanation: Correct. Local exception handling takes precedence: an applicable `@ExceptionHandler` method defined on the controller itself is selected before Spring MVC looks at any globally-scoped `@ControllerAdvice` handlers.

references.title: Spring Framework Reference — Web MVC, Controller Advice (global @ExceptionHandler methods are applied after local ones)
